parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This file passes. UserController is an Express HTTP adapter in the infrastructure layer. Its work is transport and wiring: it sets up routes, reads the request body, returns HTTP status codes, maps errors to JSON responses and wires the use case to its repository. All of these belong in infrastructure.

The `!name` check in POST /users is request-shape validation that produces a 400 response. That is normal transport-level input checking, not a domain invariant or business policy. The real creation logic is handed off to `CreateUserUseCase.execute`.

One minor concern is the GET /users handler. It calls `userRepository.findAll()` directly instead of going through an application use case, then maps the result to an `{id, name}` response object. That skips the application layer for this read. But it contains no business rule (no filtering, authorization or policy), and the mapping to a response format is a presentation/transport job. So it is a design-quality issue rather than a responsibility from a different layer kind sitting in this file. No persistence implementation, domain rules or application orchestration with business decisions appear in the file.
